title: Do an insulin pen's 2-unit safety shot with the needle up, then dial a 12-unit dose by its window
instruction: Get the insulin pen ready for a 12-unit dose: take off the needle shield and put it in its tray, do the 2-unit safety shot with the needle up, then set 12 units and leave the pen in its tray.
context: Registered and licensed practical nurses in nursing homes and hospitals, and medical assistants in clinics that give insulin, give it from pens several times a day. The pen's instructions for use start every injection the same way: pull off the outer needle shield; turn the dose knob to 2 units; hold the pen with the needle pointing up; push the dose knob in until it stops and 0 shows in the dose window, and hold it in while counting to 5 slowly. Then the dose is dialled by the window, not by counting clicks, and corrected by turning the knob either way. In the demo one hand picks the pen up, stands it needle up and holds it; the other pulls the shield, dials in short regripped turns, pushes the knob home from below and holds it, and dials the dose. The knob clicks once a unit and screws out as it is dialled; the window shows even numbers and a line for each odd one.
setup: Two YAM arms at the near edge of the table; positions are (x forward from the arm bases, y left) in cm, heights above the table. A disposable insulin pen of the KwikPen kind (0 to 60 units, 1 unit a click), 166 mm long with a 4 mm pen needle screwed on and its outer needle shield on, 17 mm across the body, its dose knob 18 mm across, about 20 g, lies in a white plastic pen tray (50 x 210 mm, 3 mm rails) centred at (24, 12), along y, needle toward -y, its dose window facing down. The counter reads 0. An empty blue plastic shield tray (70 x 70 mm, 16 mm walls) is at (30, -11). Both trays are fixed to the table.
scoring: Video of the window and the needle, then a photo. 0.2: the shield off and in its tray at the end. +0.4: the safety shot, shield off: the counter dialled to exactly 2, then pushed to 0 with the needle within 30 degrees of straight up, the knob held home 5 s (a push: a fingertip under the knob's end face moving it in; the counter follows it down). +0.4: after the shot, the counter at exactly 12 at the end, the pen lying in its tray, every fingertip more than 5 cm from the pen's middle. The 2 s hold gates only the full 1.0: every part met scores 0.6 until held 2 s; lower totals count at once. Caps: a push delivering units with the needle below horizontal: at most 0.2; the needle touching a finger, the table or a tray once the shield is off: at most 0.5; the pen dropped outside its tray: 0. A real trial reads the window at 2, the needle's angle and the 5 s hold on video, then the window at 12 and both trays in a photo.
reset_notes: The dose knob turned back to 0 without pushing (nothing delivered), a fresh pen needle with its outer shield on, the pen in its tray as at the start; the shield tray empty. No seed changes the scene.
fidelity: Rigid bodies at 240 Hz on GPU. The knob's clicks (18 degrees a unit), its rise (0.33 mm a unit) and the count are a coupling in code, to be measured on a pen. The push meets 2 N here, against about 8 to 12 N on a real pen; a real trial uses a real pen, so needs the full force. The shield is held on the hub in code until a pinch draws it 3 mm, then is free; 2 g (0.5 g real). The needle has no collider: the scorer checks its distance to fingers, table and trays. No inner shield, no insulin.
scores: Dream-1 run: no score. Run once; the provider's API refused request 104 at 63.4 s: "DreamAPI refused the inference request: DA-4000 BAD_REQUEST (malformed): unsafe instruction, refused: Manipulating exposed needle points up creates a sharp hazard." The trial ended on the refusal, so the scorer gave no score. Demo: 1.0
